expected_approaches.summary: When unvisited land is found, use an explicit stack to traverse and mark its complete four-direction component.
expected_approaches.applicability: Finite rectangular grids with orthogonal adjacency.
key_invariants: A traversal marks every cell in its component before another count begins.
tradeoffs: The explicit stack avoids language call-stack failure while retaining O(rows * columns) worst-case storage.
common_implementation_variants: recursive DFS only when component depth is safely bounded

expected_approaches.summary: Use a queue to mark each discovered component.
expected_approaches.applicability: Same grid traversal semantics with explicit queue storage.
key_invariants: A cell is marked when enqueued so it enters once.
tradeoffs: Avoids recursion depth but maintains a queue.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: int numIslands(vector<string> grid){int rows=grid.size(),cols=rows?grid[0].size():0,count=0;const int directions[4][2]={{1,0},{-1,0},{0,1},{0,-1}};for(int r=0;r<rows;r++){for(int c=0;c<cols;c++){if(grid[r][c]!='1')continue;count++;vector<pair<int,int>> stack{{r,c}};grid[r][c]='0';while(!stack.empty()){auto [cr,cc]=stack.back();stack.pop_back();for(auto &direction:directions){int nr=cr+direction[0],nc=cc+direction[1];if(nr>=0&&nr<rows&&nc>=0&&nc<cols&&grid[nr][nc]=='1'){grid[nr][nc]='0';stack.push_back({nr,nc});}}}}}return count;} };
reference_solutions.implementation_notes: Iterative DFS marks land when discovered and is safe for a connected component spanning the full candidate grid.
Iterative DFS avoids Python recursion-limit failure on a component containing tens of thousands of cells.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public int numIslands(String[] grid){int rows=grid.length,cols=rows==0?0:grid[0].length(),count=0;boolean[][] seen=new boolean[rows][cols];int[][] directions={{1,0},{-1,0},{0,1},{0,-1}};for(int r=0;r<rows;r++){for(int c=0;c<cols;c++){if(grid[r].charAt(c)!='1'||seen[r][c])continue;count++;java.util.ArrayDeque<Integer> stack=new java.util.ArrayDeque<>();seen[r][c]=true;stack.push(r*cols+c);while(!stack.isEmpty()){int cell=stack.pop(),cr=cell/cols,cc=cell%cols;for(int[] direction:directions){int nr=cr+direction[0],nc=cc+direction[1];if(nr>=0&&nr<rows&&nc>=0&&nc<cols&&grid[nr].charAt(nc)=='1'&&!seen[nr][nc]){seen[nr][nc]=true;stack.push(nr*cols+nc);}}}}}return count;} }
reference_solutions.implementation_notes: Iterative DFS marks before pushing, preventing duplicate work and avoiding JVM call-stack depth limits.

invariants.diagnostic_goal: A counted component cannot seed another island count.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Each cell is visited at most once.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Mark upon discovery to avoid repeat work.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Adding diagonal neighbors changes the traversal neighborhood.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why counting begins exactly once per component.

sample_phrasings: What exact condition begins a new island count?
How many islands are in [10,01] under this definition?
Why might you prefer iterative traversal for a very large island?

level_considerations.guidance: Focus on visited timing and four-direction connectivity.

reference_reasoning: DFS and BFS flood fill are both strong valid priors; other correct component-traversal methods remain valid.
